title: Output Jailbreaking Guardrails
summary: Apply an explicit output policy before publication and prevent unsafe model content from becoming executable instructions or unauthorized business actions.
overview: Output guardrails inspect generated content against the application's publication and action policies. They may detect disallowed content, sensitive-data exposure, unsupported claims, or attempts to evade restrictions through encoding and role-play. The title describes a defense boundary; no guardrail can guarantee that every jailbreak attempt will fail.

Distinguish output moderation from tool authorization. A harmless-looking explanation can accompany an unauthorized tool call, while a quoted harmful phrase may be legitimate evidence in a security workflow. Evaluate content in context, enforce action controls independently, and define whether the system blocks, transforms, escalates, or returns a constrained alternative.

production.poc: A prototype can test a small policy set with benign and adversarial examples. Include legitimate discussion of sensitive material to reveal overblocking.
production.production: Production combines structural validation, sensitive-data checks, semantic classification, and application-specific rules before delivery. Streaming responses require a deliberate buffering or incremental-check policy.
production.scale: At scale, version policy and classifiers, evaluate multilingual and encoded attacks, and monitor false positives by workflow. Classifier availability and latency must have explicit degraded behavior.

components.name: Output policy
components.role: Defines allowed content, protected data, action constraints, and response handling by use case.

components.name: Validation pipeline
components.role: Applies schema, secret, evidence, and semantic checks with documented ordering.

components.name: Decision engine
components.role: Combines guardrail results into allow, block, transform, or review outcomes.

components.name: Safe response adapter
components.role: Produces a constrained alternative without repeating the rejected sensitive payload.

components.name: Evaluation corpus
components.role: Maintains benign edge cases, known bypasses, and policy-version regression tests.

flow.title: Collect candidate
flow.description: Hold the generated response or a policy-defined streaming segment before publication.

flow.title: Validate structure
flow.description: Reject malformed or unexpected fields before semantic checks operate on them.

flow.title: Inspect content
flow.description: Evaluate sensitive data, disallowed requests, and application-specific output conditions.

flow.title: Apply context
flow.description: Distinguish quoted evidence and legitimate professional discussion from prohibited assistance.

flow.title: Choose response
flow.description: Allow, redact, block, or escalate according to explicit policy and detector confidence.

flow.title: Record outcome
flow.description: Log reason codes and minimal evidence for evaluation without reproducing sensitive content unnecessarily.

useCase.title: Moderating a student support assistant
useCase.situation: An education platform offers tutoring and administrative assistance to students in different age groups.
useCase.problem: Adversarial prompts can solicit inappropriate content, while simplistic keyword filters block legitimate literature and safety discussions.
useCase.requirement: The assistant must apply the platform's age-appropriate policy without exposing private student records or suppressing necessary educational context.
useCase.architecture: A guardrail pipeline checks output structure, personal-data exposure, and contextual policy before the response is displayed.
runtime: A generated answer is evaluated against the student's authorized service context and the current tutoring policy.
If rejected, a response adapter offers a permitted educational direction without echoing the problematic content.
useCase.failure: If the semantic classifier is unavailable, sensitive workflows use a constrained fallback or review path defined by policy.
useCase.impact: Measure policy violations, legitimate-content rejection, added latency, and bypass success across supported languages and age-appropriate evaluation sets.

tradeoffs.benefit: Context can reduce crude keyword overblocking.
tradeoffs.cost: Classifiers add latency and remain fallible.

tradeoffs.benefit: Full responses can be checked before exposure.
Useful content can survive limited redaction.
tradeoffs.cost: Transformation may change meaning and needs revalidation.

failures.scenario: Sensitive text leaks in an early streaming chunk
failures.detection: Delivery trace shows publication before policy evaluation.
failures.recovery: Buffer protected content or apply an explicitly tested incremental strategy.

failures.detection: Adversarial evaluation finds a policy-violating decoded payload.
failures.recovery: Improve normalization and strengthen downstream publication controls.

mistakes.fix: Inspect actual content and external actions.

mistakes.mistake: Using one policy for every audience
mistakes.fix: Apply the relevant product and user context.
Store minimal reason codes and protected evidence references.

whenToUse: Generated content reaches users or downstream systems.
The application has explicit content and data policies.
Contextual review can distinguish legitimate edge cases.
whenNotToUse: The control is expected to replace authorization.
A proposed detector is treated as a complete safety guarantee.
checklist: Define allow, block, transform, and review outcomes.
